message.content:
Sure! Here’s a quick way to post that comment to VirusTotal using a simple `curl` command (or a short Python snippet if you prefer).  
Just replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with your actual key (`ABC321` in this case) and run it from a terminal.

---

## 1. Using `curl`

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
           "type": "comment",
           "attributes": {
             "text": "Confirmed #malware"
           }
         }'
```

**What it does**

- `POST /api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments` – creates a new comment on the IP resource.
- `x-apikey` header authenticates you.
- The JSON payload is exactly what you supplied.

If everything goes well, you’ll get a `201 Created` response with the comment details.

---

## 2. Using Python (requests)

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"
headers = {
    "x-apikey": "ABC321",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
        "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
}

response = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(response.status_code)
print(response.json())
```

Make sure you have the `requests` library installed (`pip install requests`).

---

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | API key (`ABC321`) |
| ✅ | IP address (`192.168.1.1`) |
| ✅ | Comment JSON (`{"type":"comment","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"}}`) |
| ✅ | Correct endpoint (`/api/v3/ip_addresses/<ip>/comments`) |
| ✅ | `x-apikey` header |
